title: The Common Aches of Pregnancy
hook: Nausea, heartburn, fatigue, and a sore back are the everyday companions of pregnancy — usually normal and manageable. The skill is knowing the simple fixes, and which symptoms are not on this list.
key_points: Morning sickness (nausea, often any time of day) is common in early pregnancy and usually eases after the first trimester; small, frequent meals and ginger can help.
Heartburn, constipation, fatigue, back pain, and swollen feet are typical as pregnancy progresses.
Simple measures help: frequent small meals, fluids and fiber, gentle movement, good support, and rest when you can.
Some symptoms are NOT just discomfort — severe or constant vomiting, heavy bleeding, a bad headache, or sudden swelling need prompt medical advice.
content_html: Pregnancy reshapes the whole body, and a string of everyday discomforts comes with the territory. Early on, the headliner is nausea — "morning sickness" that can strike at any hour. It's very common, tends to ease after the first trimester, and often responds to small, frequent meals, keeping something in your stomach, and remedies like ginger. As the weeks go on, other familiar aches tend to arrive: heartburn, constipation, deep fatigue, back pain, and swelling in the feet and ankles.
extra_html: Most of these are normal and manageable with simple adjustments — eating little and often, drinking plenty of water and getting enough fiber, staying gently active, using good back and belly support, and resting when your body asks. What matters just as much is knowing where the line is, because not every symptom belongs on the "normal" list. Severe or relentless vomiting that stops you keeping fluids down, vaginal bleeding, a severe headache or vision changes, or sudden swelling are signals to contact your midwife or doctor rather than wait them out. This is general guidance — your maternity team can advise on relief that's safe in pregnancy and check anything that worries you.

related.title: Eating Well When You're Pregnant
related.hook: Most foods are fine in pregnancy — but a short list carries infection or toxin risks worth knowing, alongside a daily folic acid supplement and a varied, balanced diet.

related.title: Pregnancy Symptoms to Never Ignore
related.hook: A few symptoms in pregnancy mean call your midwife or maternity unit straight away — they can signal serious problems like pre-eclampsia that need checking without delay.
